parameterized_or_safe_query_construction.title: Parameterized / Safe Query Construction
parameterized_or_safe_query_construction.description: Attestation: every statement, command, or query issued on this data flow is built via a parameterized/prepared/safe-binding API for whatever engine speaks here - SQL prepared statements ($1/$2 placeholders, PreparedStatement, named-binding ORM), MongoDB query-object/operator binding (not string-built $where/JS), Cassandra/CQL bound statements, Elasticsearch/OpenSearch parameterized query DSL, Cypher parameters ($param, not string-built) for Neo4j/Memgraph, and Redis argument arrays rather than untrusted EVAL/Lua - so query/command structure and user-supplied values travel as separate fields. When false, untrusted input can alter the query/command structure (UNION SELECT, NoSQL operator injection, CQL/Cypher injection, RESP/Lua injection) and the flow's own legitimate result channel becomes a bulk-exfiltration path. Verified by code review and SAST on every query/command-construction path in the data-access layer. Grounded in OWASP Top 10 2021 A03 Injection.

untrusted_input_concatenated_into_query_.title: Untrusted Input Concatenated Into Query Or Command
untrusted_input_concatenated_into_query_.description: Attestation: at least one code path on this data flow builds the query, command, or filter by concatenating or interpolating untrusted input directly (SQL/CQL/Cypher string-building, MongoDB operator/JSON injection, Elasticsearch/OpenSearch query-DSL string concatenation, or Redis CRLF/command or EVAL/Lua injection). When true, the engine cannot distinguish data from structure and the path is exploitable for injection regardless of any sibling validation. Independent of parameterized_or_safe_query_construction because a flow may use safe binding on most paths while still concatenating on one outlier helper; both triggers are kept so either failure mode fires the exposure.

flow_tls_encrypted.title: Flow TLS Encrypted
flow_tls_encrypted.description: Attestation: the application-to-database flow is TLS-encrypted end to end (PostgreSQL hostssl + sslmode>=require on the client; MySQL REQUIRE SSL; managed equivalents enforce in-transit encryption). When false, every query and every result-set row traverses the wire in plaintext and is readable by any on-path attacker (rogue VPC node, compromised network appliance, mis-scoped peering).

data_tier_transit_encrypted.title: Data-Tier Transit Encrypted
data_tier_transit_encrypted.description: Canonical workspace attestation that the data-tier transport (this DB flow's underlying channel) is encrypted in transit — the cross-class twin of flow_tls_encrypted shared with API Call / gateway flows so a single workspace baseline drives both. When false, the cleartext-sniffing exposure fires on this flow.

server_certificate_validated.title: Server Certificate Validated
server_certificate_validated.description: Attestation: the application validates the database server's TLS certificate (full chain-of-trust AND hostname/identity, e.g. PostgreSQL sslmode=verify-full with sslrootcert pinned, JDBC sslVerifyServerCertificate=true / VERIFY_IDENTITY) before sending credentials or queries. False when the driver is configured with sslmode=require/prefer/allow, verify-ca without hostname check, or a custom TrustManager that trusts any certificate — at which point an on-path attacker can terminate TLS with a self-signed cert and harvest credentials and result rows.

tls_root_trust_managed.title: TLS Root Trust Managed
tls_root_trust_managed.description: Attestation: the TLS trust anchor used by the client for this flow is a pinned, narrowly-scoped CA bundle (e.g. sslrootcert pointing at the specific CA that signed the DB, or an internal PKI root) rather than the OS-wide public trust store or no trust anchor at all. False when the client trusts any cert chained to any public CA, has an empty/unmanaged trust store, or uses a 'trust all certs' TrustManager — which collapses certificate validation even if sslmode is nominally set to verify-full.

per_workload_db_identity_used.title: Per-Workload DB Identity Used
per_workload_db_identity_used.description: Attests that the application authenticates to the database as its OWN distinct DB principal (per-workload login role) rather than via a shared service account or root/superuser. Per-workload identity is the precondition for credible audit attribution and least-privilege scoping on this dataFlow; a shared account collapses blast-radius and accountability, and makes a leaked credential indistinguishable from any sibling workload. Secure when true.

data_tier_credentials_short_lived.title: Data-Tier Credentials Short-Lived
data_tier_credentials_short_lived.description: Attests that the DB credentials used on this flow are short-lived and broker-issued (Vault dynamic database secrets, RDS/Cloud SQL IAM auth tokens, X.509 short-life certs) with a bounded TTL (<= 24h) and revoke-on-shutdown, rather than a static long-lived password persisted in .env, a k8s Secret, or git history. Static long-lived DB passwords are the dominant root cause of post-breach lateral movement to the data tier — a single .env exfiltration grants indefinite, fully-impersonating access on this flow. Secure when true.

least_privilege_db_account.title: Least-Privilege DB Account
least_privilege_db_account.description: Attestation: the DB principal used on this application-to-database flow holds ONLY the rights its workload requires — per-object grants scoped to the specific tables and verbs the workload actually issues, with rolsuper=f / rolcreatedb=f / rolcreaterole=f / rolbypassrls=f and no membership in catch-all roles. True when grants are object-scoped; false when the principal holds SUPERUSER, db_owner, or GRANT ALL (CIS PostgreSQL Benchmark — least-privilege role attributes; PostgreSQL 18 GRANT reference). When false, any application-side bug that lets an attacker run one DB call lets them run any DB call — including dumping every table or creating a backdoor role.

bulk_read_volume_anomaly_alerted.title: Bulk-Read Volume Anomaly Alerted
bulk_read_volume_anomaly_alerted.description: Attestation that out-of-band anomaly detection (DAM, RDS/Cloud SQL Performance Insights, or SIEM rule) watches this database-query flow for per-principal volume spikes (rows returned / bytes shipped) and routes alerts to an on-call owner. When false, a single SELECT * over a large table — accidental or weaponised via SQLi / stolen credential / insider — leaves through this legitimate flow as one 'normal' query response with no one watching.

bulk_export_monitored_and_alerted.title: Bulk Export Monitored and Alerted
bulk_export_monitored_and_alerted.description: Attestation that bulk-export operations on this flow (large result sets, multi-table breadth, or sustained high-row-count fetches per principal) are continuously monitored with a defined threshold and alert routing — the OWASP API Security 'per-account quota / volume anomaly' compensating control for cases where in-app LIMIT caps are bypassed. When false, exfiltration via the legitimate query channel is indistinguishable from normal traffic.

pii_excluded_from_logs.title: PII Excluded from Logs
pii_excluded_from_logs.description: Attestation: raw PII (card numbers, emails, SSNs, names) bound into query parameters is NOT written to the database/driver log store. Secure when pgaudit.log_parameter is OFF in production AND the application's driver/ORM SQL-logging layer is set to log statement text only (no bind values), so a breach of the log store does not become a parallel breach of the PII table. Fires when raw bind values are mirrored into logs.

secrets_masked_in_logs.title: Secrets Masked in Logs
secrets_masked_in_logs.description: Attestation: secret material that may appear in queries on this flow (auth tokens, API keys, password-reset tokens passed as bind values, encryption keys) is masked or excluded in any captured query/error log. Secure when the log pipeline scrubs/masks known secret fields before persistence. Fires when secrets traverse this flow as raw bind values and reach the log store unredacted.

data_store_publicly_routable.title: Data Store Publicly Routable
data_store_publicly_routable.description: Interpreted attestation: the database endpoint serving this flow is reachable from the public internet — its security group / firewall allows 0.0.0.0/0 (or ::/0) on the DB port, OR listen_addresses is bound to all interfaces on a publicly-routable NIC. Secure value is false (the DB sits in a private subnet / is only reachable from the app tier). When true, mass internet scanners discover the listener within hours and credential-stuff against any known/leaked role — the precondition for the public-listener brute-force vector.

data_tier_ingress_scoped_per_workload_id.title: Data-Tier Ingress Scoped Per Workload Identity
data_tier_ingress_scoped_per_workload_id.description: Interpreted attestation: ingress to the data tier on this flow is constrained to the specific application workload's identity — security-group source is the app-tier SG (not 0.0.0.0/0, not a shared bastion SG, not a broad VPC CIDR), and pg_hba.conf / equivalent restricts the source range to that workload. Secure value is true. When false, any host that can reach the VPC (or the internet) can attempt the DB port — the network half of the brute-force precondition that pairs with data_store_publicly_routable.
